study type: Secondary analysis of prospective cohort data
exposure: Type of caesarean section (unplanned/emergency vs. planned)
cohort: 354 mother-child dyads from the Alberta Pregnancy Outcomes and Nutrition (APrON) study (2009-2013)
finding: Emergency caesarean section was indirectly associated with increased PPD symptoms, mediated through PTSD symptoms.
mod_finding: Mothers who had an emergency C-section had higher PTSD scores, which in turn was associated with higher PPD symptoms.
